author: kesudh
method: Exact shortest-path-tree warm refinement: radix A*, feasible per-sink bounds, neutral and group reroutes, preserved-route and displacement-chain repair, optional circular integer buckets, multiple CPU search workers, strict final-walk polishing, and exact two-parent minimum-cut crossover following PR24. Our GPU kernels are audited prototypes and did not generate these refinements; selected PR26 public warm starts are attributed to its GPU-accelerated engine. Bounded conflict-based search over static multi-sink trees, alternated with neutral group reroutes; opt-in specialized chain pricing avoids full-grid cost setup. 2026-10-04 adoption update: 4 case(s) where a merged entry's route is strictly better than this entry's previous route are carried verbatim from coordinated_refinement (main 2566f5f1); documented as "retained public route" in the cases list, credited via derived_from.

derived_from.author: Leonid Popryho
derived_from.warm_started_from: coordinated_refinement (jay-tau) and its upstream entries; cases refined here were warm-started from the published route for that case
derived_from.note: Per-case provenance is byte-verified: each shipped route is compared with every published entry's file and credited to the one it matches. Routes matching none are this entry's own refinement.

runtime_hardware: Windows, Intel i7-13700HX, 16 cores/24 threads; actual worker count recorded per command; concurrent Hermes and benchmark workloads. Observed wall times, not normalized.
selection: The best independently legal output per case, as reported by the official checker; ties keep the earlier route. Timed multiworker search is nondeterministic, so a repeat can return a different legal route.

algorithm_references.method: conflict splitting, adapted to static vertex-disjoint multi-sink trees
algorithm_references.citation: Sharon, Stern, Felner and Sturtevant, Conflict-based search for optimal multi-agent pathfinding

hardware: 13th Gen Intel Core i7-13700HX (16 cores / 24 threads), 31.7 GB RAM, Windows 11
runtime_scope: Per case, `runtime.json` reports the wall-clock seconds of one end-to-end run of this entry's router on that case: the benchmark instance in, the shipped route as the warm start, a refined .sol.json out, at a fixed 30 s search budget on 4 worker threads (chain-fast mode, 2-8 sink groups). The engine self-reports the elapsed time and that number is recorded. All 45 cases were re-measured the same way, so the column is uniform and comparable. Own-refined cases: the shipped bytes were produced by a run of this type (earlier runs used the same operators at case-specific budgets). Cases whose shipped bytes are a credited public entry's file carried verbatim: the reported time is this entry's own run on that instance, not the upstream author's generation time, which is not claimed. Runs are sequential per case but several cases were measured concurrently, so wall-clock values are conservative.
